title: Engine Controls — Thrust Lever Quadrant — In-Situ Measurement of the Detent Breakout Force
abstract: In-situ measurement of the thrust lever detent breakout force on high-hour aircraft, to identify the quadrants that need the seal and friction clamp change before a crew report is raised.

sections.planning_reason: Crew reports of a soft or absent detent at the climb gate rose steadily from 2015 and reached one hundred and forty in 2017, concentrated on aircraft above twenty thousand flight hours. The cause is lubricant displaced from the detent onto the friction clamp faces, which then slip. The condition develops gradually and the first indication today is a crew report, which is late and inconsistent between crews. This bulletin puts a number on the condition so that the quadrant change can be planned rather than reacted to.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin is a measurement only. The detent breakout force is measured at the climb gate and at the flex gate on each lever with a calibrated gauge, in both directions, and the readings are compared against the acceptance band given in the instructions. Quadrants outside the band are identified for the seal and clamp change. Nothing is dismantled and nothing is fitted. How many aircraft the measurement will find is not yet known; the band was set from a sample of twelve strip-downs.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Make sure that the engines are shut down, that the aircraft is on ground power and that the autothrust is disconnected. Get access to the flight compartment in zones 211 and 215; the centre pedestal does not have to be opened. Fit the calibrated force gauge to the lever knob using the supplied adapter. Move the lever slowly from idle towards the climb gate and record the force at which the detent breaks out. Repeat in the opposite direction. Repeat both directions at the flex gate. Repeat the full sequence on the second lever. Compare every reading with the acceptance band and record the result on the attached form. If any reading is below the lower limit, plan the quadrant change bulletin at the next opportunity. Report the readings to Aeralis so that the fleet distribution can be maintained.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all ZEPHYR-18, ZEPHYR-20, ZEPHYR-22 and ZEPHYR-24 aircraft that have not had the seal and friction clamp change embodied. Aircraft delivered from the production cut-in are at the modified standard and do not need the measurement.
sections.material_note: No kit is required. The calibrated force gauge and the lever adapter are available on loan from Aeralis and are returned after use. No consumables are needed.

type_data.compliance_time: Once, at the next opportunity, on aircraft above 20000 flight hours. Repeat every 6000 flight hours until the quadrant change is embodied.

abstract: In-situ measurement of the thrust lever detent breakout force on high-hour aircraft, re-issued with the measured fleet population that falls below the acceptance band and the confirmation that the band is unchanged.
